title: New York Magazine: May 9–22, 2022

description.main: The May 9–22, 2022 issue of New York magazine, with a cover by Barbara Kruger asking "Who becomes a 'murderer' in post-Roe America?"
description.extended:
The May 9–22, 2022 issue of New York magazine, with a cover by Barbara Kruger asking "Who becomes a 'murderer' in post-Roe America?"

The issue appeared as the Supreme Court looked set to overturn Roe v. Wade, and it examines what the end of legal abortion would mean for American life. Kruger reworked her 1989 silkscreen Untitled (Your body is a battleground), keeping its face split into positive and negative halves and setting the new question in white on red bars. She told the magazine she put "murderer" in quotes because it is the language of the right, and asked who is punished in a world where abortion is murder.

Inside, Kerry Howley profiles Susan B. Anthony List president Marjorie Dannenfelser, Rebecca Traister writes on how abortion's illegality would affect everyone, and Irin Carmon reports on the threats facing the abortion funds that help low-income people get care.
description.artist_bio: Barbara Kruger (b. 1945, Newark) is an American conceptual artist associated with the Pictures Generation. After working as a designer and picture editor at Conde Nast magazines, she began in the late 1970s to pair found black-and-white photographs with declarative text in Futura Bold Oblique, white on red. The Barbara Kruger Catalogue Raisonne (barbarakruger.org) documents the work; she is represented by Sprueth Magers and David Zwirner.
